_scenario: Multi-country European rollout: one en-gb base package, with de-de, fr-fr, es-es, it-it and nl-nl added per user group.
_readThisFirst: Language is a SCALAR, not a list. There is no 'Languages' array, and a JSON array here does not work - the build coerces it to the string 'de-de fr-fr' and hard-fails with "value 'de-de fr-fr' is not in the registered KnownValues set" before anything is staged. That is a deliberate design choice rather than a limitation to work around: each additional UI language adds roughly 300-400 MB to the payload that EVERY device downloads, so baking five languages into the base package would make every device pay for all five.
_howMultiLanguageActuallyWorks: 1. Pick ONE base UI language below. It sets the Shell UI - Start menu shortcuts, right-click context menus, tooltips - and Microsoft requires an uninstall and reinstall of Office to change it later, so it is worth getting right first time.
2. Build once. That single .intunewin serves every country; nothing about it is country-specific except the base language.

3. Ship each additional language as its own Intune Win32 app from Build\Output\LanguagePacks\, targeted at the group that needs it. The same .intunewin is reused for every language - only the command parameters and the uploaded detection script differ.

4. Give each language app a dependency on Microsoft 365 Apps with Auto-install = Yes, and leave it OUT of the ESP blocking list. Users then reach the desktop while their language pack installs behind them.
_baseLanguageChoice: en-gb is used here as a neutral base for a European tenant. If one country dominates, use its language instead and ship en-gb as one of the packs - the pattern is the same either way.

_additionalLanguageApps._comment: One Intune Win32 app per language. These are NOT build-config values - they are listed here so the whole rollout is described in one place. All five are supported for Microsoft 365 Apps, Visio and Project.
_additionalLanguageApps._detectionScript: Build\Output\LanguagePacks\DetectionScripts\Detect-LanguagePack-<LanguageID>.ps1 - upload the wrapper matching the language; Intune runs detection scripts with no parameters, which is why one pre-generated wrapper exists per language.
_additionalLanguageApps._dependency: Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise, Auto-install = Yes

_ifYouAlsoDeployVisioOrProject: Visio and Project base installs are always en-us, independent of the Language token. To give them a European language, add a second LanguagePack app per language with -TargetProduct VisioProRetail or ProjectProRetail. All five languages above are in the Visio and Project matrices.
